items.title: Zeke Mullins interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 9, 2017
items.q: You’re going from Beethoven to Teddy Wilson, right?

ctx.x: Well let’s see. I think Benny Goodman was probably — he was one of the top, I’d say top musicians playing. He wasn’t actually playing jazz though, he was playing swing, which, it sounded close to jazz. And I used to listen to his band you know, with Teddy Wilson playing piano. And he had that extra group, a sextet I think it was, and Lionel Hampton was in that group. And I mean it really excited me. You know I started talking about this, and well my mother and father, I have to confess they weren’t really into…
You’re going from Beethoven to Teddy Wilson, right?

It was a long ways. But you know I just kept it up. And a lot of the stuff that I came from, I taught myself you know? Because I bought these books. I could play scales and stuff, but then I came to realize that the chords in jazz were built on the scales. So if you understood your scale then it really wasn’t that hard to understand the distance of the notes playing chords you know. Excuse me [gets up] Because the guys would say you play the right single notes but you don’t play the right chords. And so you…
